blocks.text: תולעתא. In the Jerusalem Talmud (Sabbat C. 1. fol. 3b) it is said: In seven years the תולעתא דסוסייא (maggot from the carcass of the horse) becomes אירעי (hornets), and the דתורתא (maggot from the ox) becomes דברי (bees); with this cf. Aelian (Thiergesch. 1, 28), who says the same of the wasps (Σφῆκες [Sphēkes]) and (ibid. 2, 57) of the bees (Μέλισσαι [Melissai]); the latter, according to an ancient belief, are said to arise from the remains of the carcass of the ox. On the various opinions concerning the origin of the bees, cf. also Aristotle (Thierg. 5, 18); in accordance with that legend, that the bees arise from the putrefaction of oxen, they are also called in Greek Βούπαιδες [Boupaides], Βουγενές [Bougenes] and Βουποιητοί [Boupoiētoi].

In our passage it further says: רב פדה חד אפר מתעביד שר מומית' דרוש' מתעביד עקרבי ודמניא שממי, words which I am unable to explain; they will presumably read differently in a correct edition. Should רמניא perhaps be read [p. 376] for רמניא? The Μαῖα [Maia] (Aristotle l. c. 4, 2, 2) is the sea crab, which some call the sea spider because of its resemblance to the spider. Thus in French it is called Araignée de mer; the Ligurians called it outright Aranea; see Scaliger on Aristot. 4, 3, 2, and thus that fabulous notion of the metamorphosis may have arisen.

On §. 20 it should be noted that the castrated ox is suited to the plough because castration makes it more docile (not stronger, as Pliny h. n. 8, 26 mistakenly thinks); cf. Reynier: De l'économie publique et rurale des anciens peuples (German translation by Rau) p. 86.

In §. 136, p. 104, l. 12 from the top, it should read: “since both, the raven and the bat, live on cereals as well as on animal food; on the raven cf. in particular Pliny (h. n. 17, 5, 4 and below p. 173).”

In §. 165, p. 141, l. 2 from above, it should read: “Out of hunger it once devoured a fish; according to Niebuhr (Beschreibung Arabiens p. 255 and p. 269) the nomads on the Persian Gulf even feed their cattle with dried fish.
Since it does not, like the ox, let saliva flow while eating” etc.
p. 6 l. 1 from bottom מפוני read מפניו.
Some other easily recognizable misprints the reader is asked to excuse on account of the author's great distance from the place of printing.
